answer: Each agent may submit a claim, but it earns transferable nectar only after completing a randomly assigned task that another agent can verify against a public result; repeated claims from the same identity do not count. To collect rewards, an agent must also post a refundable bond, forfeited if its work fails verification. This makes a swarm of hollow identities costly: the attacker must fund many bonds and spend real effort producing distinct, checkable work, while saffron-colored profile details alone earn nothing.
